newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares see new highs, no drop seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares see new highs, no drop seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares hit new highs on Thursday amid domestic investor enthusiasm, traders said, seeing the momentum continuing at least to the end of the week, although they disagreed whether Western money was at play.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index rose to its third consecutive record close at 559.86 on a record $120.7 million total market turnover. The index closed on Wednesday at a record 533.86.
"When clients are willing to buy and say they'll take the offer price, what else can the market do but rise?" said Prospekt chief of securities trading Andrei Ippolitov.
He said Russian demand was still the main force on the market, and saw smaller investors buying, while bigger players were decreasing buying and selling.
But Raiffeisenbank Austria equities chief Sergei Sheikov said Western demand was still very active.
"Russian money of course is underpinning, and often supporting the market, but there is also good money from the West, mostly from the U.S.A.," he said.
Fund flows are often the determining factor in sharp rises in the illiquid Russian shares market.
"In the first half of the day there was good demand from London -- no offers just bids -- and after New York opened the same thing seemed to start happening."

Oil company LUKoil LKOH.RTS closed at a record $28.02 after $24.90 on Wednesday, regional utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS rose to $1.760 from $1.620 and oil company Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS rose to $1.32 from $1.27.
Traders said they saw no end to the rise for now.

"Of course the new levels are driving everyone out of their minds, but it is completely possible that the market will go even further -- either capital is being transferred (from the West) or people are expecting it to happen," said Sheikov.
"Everyone is reducing their holdings in the States."
